Open Vermont on the map

Key dates

  • Early voting window (in person or by mail): September 19, 2026 to November 2, 2026. Early voting starts 45 days before a statewide general election. You can vote early in person at your town clerk's office during office hours.
  • Last day to request a mail ballot: November 2, 2026. Ballots were mailed to all active registered voters in early October. To request one, contact your town clerk by close of business the day before Election Day. Voted ballots must reach the clerk by Election Day.
  • Voter registration deadline: November 3, 2026. Vermont has same-day registration, so you can register at your polling place on Election Day. You can also register earlier at vote.vermont.gov or with your town clerk.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Polls open between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m., depending on your town, and close at 7:00 p.m.

Official election information: vote.gov

Who's running

Only the U.S. Senate and governor races are loaded so far. Other statewide offices, ballot measures, U.S. House and local races aren't loaded yet. Check your sample ballot for the full list.

Governor

The governor serves a 2-year term, and incumbent Republican Phil Scott is running again. Vermont elects the lieutenant governor in a separate race, not on a joint ticket.
